}   119	### 5.1 ATLAS-run test commands: the Docker `test-sandbox` (Phase 4 prerequisite; decision D11; revised after Codex review D1)
   120	Tests run in **Linux containers on Colima**, a Docker-compatible runtime in a Lima VM (MIT licence). Repository code never runs on the macOS host.
   121	
   122	#### 5.1.1 Runtime and VM
   123	- **Dedicated profile** `colima --profile atlas`. ATLAS always addresses it through the explicit endpoint `unix://~/.colima/atlas/docker.sock`. It never uses `DOCKER_HOST`, the current Docker context, or another daemon.
   124	- **Restricted VM mounts.** Colima shares the home directory into the VM by default. ATLAS requires the `atlas` VM to mount **nothing** from the host, because data moves only by streaming over the Docker API (§5.1.3). A dedicated, size-capped VM disk (e.g. 60 GB) keeps disk exhaustion inside the ATLAS VM.
   125	- **Repository Dockerfile builds are disabled in this release** (ATLAS-D10). Images are prebuilt, from publishers the user approves (e.g. official `python`, `node`, `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright`), and pinned by digest in ATLAS project config. Approval records publisher, tag, digest and date. Enabling builds needs a new decision and an isolated build-service design.
   126	
   127	#### 5.1.2 Candidate export (ATLAS-D03)
   128	- ATLAS builds the input tar **directly from git objects**: `git ls-tree -r -z --full-tree <candidate>` plus `git cat-file --batch`. Each entry is written with its exact path, mode (`100644`/`100755`) and, for symlinks, the link text as stored. No `.gitattributes` processing (no `export-ignore` or `export-subst`), no smudge filters, no `.git` directory.
   129	- **Unsupported entries block the run** with `BLOCKED(unsupported_repo_feature)`:
   130	  - gitlinks (submodules);
   131	  - Git LFS pointer files, or paths with `filter=lfs`;
   132	  - symlinks whose target is absolute or escapes the tree;
   133	  - paths that collide case-insensitively;
   134	  - paths over limits.
   135	
   136	  Supporting these needs a later, candidate-bound materialisation design.
   137	- ATLAS also writes the **expected manifest**: NUL-delimited `(path, type, git mode, blob id)` for every entry.
   138	
   139	#### 5.1.3 Execution layout: source immutable (ATLAS-D01)
   140	- Volume `src-<execution_id>` is populated from the tar by an ATLAS-owned **helper image** (pinned digest, built by ATLAS from a reviewed Dockerfile in this repo). It is then mounted **read-only** at `/work` in every repository-code container, setup and test alike. Repository code can't modify source at any time, including mid-run, so "swap and restore" attacks are impossible, not just detected.
   141	- **Writable locations are separate**, declared per project and approved by the user: `tests.writable_paths`, e.g. `node_modules`, `.venv`, `build`, `.pytest_cache`. Each gets its own volume or size-capped `tmpfs` mounted **over** that path. The rest of `/work` stays read-only. Tool caches go to `/tmp` (`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp/pyc`, etc.). `/out` is a separate writable volume for reports.
   142	- **Writable destinations can't overlay source (ATLAS-D21).** Each declared writable path is normalised (no `..`, no `.`, no trailing slash, case-folded collision check). It is rejected if **any component** of it is a symlink in the candidate tree, if it equals or contains a tracked path, or if it is an ancestor of one. It must name either a path absent from the candidate or an empty, untracked directory. Mount destinations are passed to Docker only after this check.
   143	- **Two attestations, two rules (ATLAS-D31).**
   144	  1. **Source volume:** exact equality with the candidate manifest. No extras, no differences.
   145	  2. **Effective view:** a canary with **exactly the same mount set** as the repository container walks `/work` as tests see it, with lstat semantics. Every tracked entry must match the manifest exactly. Entries **at or below a validated writable mountpoint** are permitted, with any content (e.g. a populated `node_modules/` or `.venv/`). Any other extra entry, or any tracked entry that differs or is hidden, is a failure.
   146	
   147	  Fixture: a successful setup-and-test run with a populated dependency directory must pass both attestations. An adversarial fixture covers a tracked `alias -> src` symlink combined with a writable path under `alias/`; the declaration must be rejected. **Projects whose tests must modify tracked files are unsupported** in this release: `BLOCKED(source_mutation_required)`.
   148	- **Attestation of source (ATLAS-D02).** Before and after each run, the helper container (read-only mount, no network) recomputes the manifest inside the Linux VM, which is case-sensitive:
   149	  - it uses `lstat`/`readlink`, never following links;
   150	  - it records type, executable mode and blob id (`git hash-object`);
   151	  - tracked entries are always compared, whatever the ignore rules say;
   152	  - any extra entries in the source volume are reported.
   153	
   154	  For the source volume, the result must equal the expected manifest byte for byte; the effective view follows rule 2 above. A difference → `invalid_source_mutated`, and the run can never satisfy G-TEST. Since the volume is read-only, a mismatch also means the boundary failed, which triggers a sandbox alert.
   155	
   156	#### 5.1.4 Container contract, verified before start (ATLAS-D06)
   157	Each repository-code container is created with:
   158	- `--network none` (or the egress profile, §5.1.6);
   159	- `--user 10001:10001`, `--cap-drop ALL`, `--security-opt no-new-privileges`;
   160	- `--read-only` rootfs, size-capped `tmpfs /tmp`;
   161	- `--pids-limit`, `--memory`, `--cpus`, `--log-driver local --log-opt max-size=…`;
   162	- no devices, never `--privileged`;
   163	- only the mounts listed in §5.1.3;
   164	- env limited to the project's declared non-secret allowlist;
   165	- labels `atlas.execution_id`, `atlas.project_id`, `atlas.role=setup|test`.
   166	
   167	The sequence for each container is **`create` → `inspect` → verify → `start`**. ATLAS verifies the effective `HostConfig` against the contract: NetworkMode, CapDrop, Privileged=false, ReadonlyRootfs, User, the exact Mounts set, SecurityOpt and limits. Any deviation means the container is deleted and the run fails closed.
   168	
   169	**Per-execution runtime attestation.** Before the first repository command of every execution, setup included, ATLAS checks:
   170	- the daemon ID and Colima VM boot ID are unchanged since the last full self-test; otherwise a full self-test is rerun;
   220	  1. lists every container labelled `atlas.execution_id=<id>`;
   221	  2. runs `docker kill`, then `docker wait`/`inspect` until none is running;
   222	  3. collects (§5.1.5);
   223	  4. removes containers and volumes.
   224	
   225	  Host process-group exit of the `docker` CLI is **not** treated as quiescence. If the daemon is unreachable, the run goes to `BLOCKED(sandbox_state_unknown)`, and no evidence is accepted until the containers are confirmed gone.
   226	- Startup reconciliation (recovery-strategy.md §3 step 3) includes orphaned `atlas.*`-labelled containers and volumes.
   227	
   228	#### 5.1.8 Resource containment (ATLAS-D08, revised)
   229	- Bounded: memory, CPU, PIDs, `tmpfs` sizes, log size, collection bytes and file counts, wall-clock time.
   230	- **Per-execution storage is enforced by fixed-size filesystems, not polling.** For each execution, ATLAS's trusted volume provisioner creates and preallocates one ext4 image file per writable area (dependency paths and `/out`) with `fallocate`, at the project's declared size. The provisioner is a helper container, the only privileged container ATLAS runs, and it runs only ATLAS code. Each image is loop-mounted inside the VM and exposed to the repository container as its writable mount. Writes beyond the size fail with `ENOSPC` **inside that execution only**; other executions and Docker's own storage are unaffected. The source volume is sized exactly to the candidate tree.
   231	- **Host capacity is reserved, not observed (ATLAS-D08 r3).** The Colima `atlas` VM's data lives on a **dedicated APFS volume** created once by the user (admin), e.g. `diskutil apfs addVolume <container> APFS AtlasSandbox -reserve 80g -quota 80g`. ATLAS points `COLIMA_HOME` (and Lima's data directory) at it. APFS *reserve* guarantees the space is set aside in the container, so other host processes can't consume it. APFS *quota* guarantees the VM can never use more. The VM disk cap (e.g. 60 GB) is below the quota. Before admitting any execution, ATLAS verifies three things:
   232	  1. the volume exists with reserve == quota ≥ the configured size (`diskutil apfs list` / `diskutil info`);
   233	  2. Colima's data path resolves onto that volume;
   234	  3. the execution's preallocation fits in the VM.
   235	
   236	  Otherwise: `BLOCKED(no_reserved_sandbox_storage)`. ATLAS's own data (`~/.atlas`, the DBs) is **not** on that volume, so sandbox growth can't touch it.
   237	- **Host volume exhaustion by other processes** (outside ATLAS's control) is detected, not prevented. If free space on the volume holding `~/.atlas` falls below 5 GB, the scheduler stops admitting work, in-flight executions are quiesced, and every project shows `BLOCKED(host_disk_low)` until space is freed. This is a separate path from guest `ENOSPC`. SQLite durability (`synchronous=FULL`) means a failed write aborts its transaction rather than corrupting state.
   238	- **VM disk full anyway** (e.g. image pulls). ATLAS stops scheduling test executions, quiesces running ones (§5.1.7), removes `atlas.*`-labelled stopped containers, volumes and loop images, and re-checks. If space is still short, every project goes to `BLOCKED(sandbox_disk_full)`, and the UI shows the cleanup steps.
   239	
   240	#### 5.1.9 Who can reach Docker (ATLAS-D05)
   241	Hiding the socket isn't enough, because any process running as the user can connect to a user-owned Unix socket. So:
   242	- **Agent processes run inside an ATLAS outer Seatbelt wrapper** (`sandbox-exec`; this is unrelated to the test sandbox). It denies file access to `~/.colima`, `~/.docker`, `~/.atlas` (except the agent's own worktree) and `/var/run/docker.sock`, and denies `network-outbound` to Unix sockets under those paths.
   243	- **Phase 2 spike obligation:** the Claude and Codex CLIs must work under this wrapper. They need network access to their providers and their own config and auth directories. The spike adds a test where an agent-launched command tries `curl --unix-socket ~/.colima/atlas/docker.sock` and must fail.
   244	- **If the CLIs can't run under the wrapper,** agent roles that can execute shell commands (Codex `workspace-write`, Claude with Bash) are `BLOCKED(no_agent_boundary)` until a separate runner identity design is approved. Read-only roles with no shell continue.
   245	- The test sandbox containers have no socket (§5.1.4).
   246	
   247	#### 5.1.10 Fail closed
   248	G-TEST can't pass, and the project shows `BLOCKED(no_test_sandbox)`, if any of these hold:
   249	- Colima `atlas` isn't running;
   250	- the VM has host mounts;
   251	- an image digest isn't approved;
   252	- attestation, the canary or the contract check fails;
   253	- the repository has an unsupported feature (§5.1.2).
   254	
   255	The UI tells the user exactly what to run. ATLAS doesn't start or reconfigure the VM itself until Phase 10 (launchd).
